9054c8400e2469f3: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 17 — The runway at Kota Kinabalu International Airport has been temporarily closed to facilitate rectification works, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) said today.
In a notice on Facebook, MAHB said a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) had been issued over the temporary closure.
“The runway will reopen once the necessary safety inspections and clearing works have been completed,” it said.
Passengers have been advised to check with their respective airlines for the latest flight status and updates.
MAHB did not provide details on the nature of the rectification works or how long the runway would remain closed.
f77e263562edc86b: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today allowed the prosecution's application to stay the hearing of additional evidence from a key prosecution witness in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor's RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid project corruption case.

A three-member panel led by Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli granted the application after deputy public prosecutor Mohd Asnawi Abu Hanipah informed the court that Rosmah did not object to the stay request.
"With the consent of both parties, we allow the application to stay the Court of Appeal's order dated Sept 1 until the prosecution's appeal is disposed of by the Federal Court.
"We hope the parties will inform the High Court of the Federal Court's decision as soon as it is delivered to facilitate case management at the High Court.

"The court has fixed Oct 7 for case management via e-Review and vacated the hearing for the main appeal originally scheduled for this October," said Azhahari, who sat with judges Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and K. Muniandy.
On Sept 1, the Court of Appeal allowed Rosmah's application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence.
The panel subsequently ordered that the additional evidence involving the 16th prosecution witness, businessman Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, be heard before a High Court judge.
Earlier, Asnawi said today's proceedings were initially fixed to hear the application to stay execution of the High Court order.

"However, this morning, the parties held discussions, and we were informed that the respondent does not object to the application to stay execution of the previous court order until the prosecution's appeal at the Federal Court is heard and decided.
"For the court's information, we filed a notice of appeal on Sept 4," said Asnawi, who appeared with DPPs Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib and Mohamad Mustaffa P Kunyalam.
Lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, representing Rosmah, confirmed that the defence had no objection.

"I confirm that there have been serious discussions regarding this application. Given that the new evidence involves a key witness in the case and the prosecution itself has given an assurance that it will expedite appeal proceedings at the Federal Court, we have no objection.

"In the interest of both parties, it is appropriate for the appeal at the Federal Court to be heard and decided first," he said, adding that parties would attend High Court proceedings this afternoon to update the court on the status.
Rosmah, 74, had applied to adduce additional evidence comprising a police report and a statutory declaration affirmed by Rayyan Radzwill.
In the statutory declaration, Rayyan Radzwill alleged that he was pressured by the prosecution during trial and presented documentary material challenging the credibility of his testimony.
On Sept 1, 2022, the High Court convicted Rosmah on three corruption charges under Section 16(a)(A) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
She was found guilty of soliciting RM187.5 million and receiving RM6.5 million from former Jepak Holdings managing director Saidi Abang Samsudin through her former aide, Datuk Rizal Mansor.
The gratification was an inducement to assist Jepak Holdings in securing a RM1.25 billion hybrid solar project from the Education Ministry to supply electricity to 369 rural schools in Sarawak.
Rosmah was sentenced to 10 years' jail for each charge, to run concurrently, and fined RM970 million. She was granted a stay of execution pending appeal.

8382df1d174efee1: KUALA LUMPUR: Lawyer Mohd Khairul Azam Abdul Aziz, also known as Buzze Azam, has failed to overturn his conviction and RM15,000 fine over an offensive Facebook post criticising the criminal justice system.
High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin dismissed Khairul Azam's appeals against both his conviction and sentence, as well as the prosecution's appeal for a heavier sentence.
Khairul Azam had been charged under Section 233(1)(a) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 over a Facebook post published on March 24, 2021.
The post was subsequently read at the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission office in Wangsa Maju at about 3.50pm the following day.
In his grounds of decision dated today, Aslam said the post went beyond expressing dissatisfaction with the administration of criminal justice.

He said although it touched on issues capable of legitimate public discussion, including prosecutorial decisions and the burden imposed on accused persons pending trial, the language used was aggressive, abusive and calculated to outrage.

"The tone and wording of the post show that it was not merely an expression of opinion on systemic weaknesses, but a targeted communication intended to disparage the institutions and officeholders named or plainly implicated," he said.
The judge said the post was directed at identifiable institutions, namely the Attorney-General's Chambers and the police, although they were not expressly named in the charge.
He rejected Khairul Azam's argument that the charge was defective as it did not identify the person or body allegedly annoyed.

Aslam said the charge, when read together with its particulars and the evidence, sufficiently conveyed the essential ingredients of the offence and enabled Khairul Azam to know the case he had to meet.
The judge also rejected the argument that the Facebook post amounted to protected criticism under Article 10 of the Federal Constitution.
"There is a clear distinction between fair criticism, even if robust, and abusive speech directed at causing insult or annoyance.
"In the present case, the post was not framed as a reasoned critique of policy, procedure, or institutional performance.
"It was a crude and insulting attack in vulgar terms," he said.
Aslam said a person could strongly criticise public institutions while remaining within the bounds of lawful speech.
"Once the language becomes a deliberate vehicle for abuse, the protection of free expression is not engaged in the same way."

The court also rejected Khairul Azam's argument that a subsequent amendment to Section 233, which changed the threshold from "offensive" to "grossly offensive", should apply retrospectively to his case.
The judge also found no merit in Khairul Azam's contention that the RM15,000 fine was manifestly excessive.
He said sentencing was primarily a matter for the trial court and an appellate court would intervene only where a sentence was plainly wrong, excessive or inadequate.
Aslam also dismissed the prosecution's appeal seeking an enhanced sentence on grounds that the RM15,000 fine remained within the range reasonably open to the trial court.
He said the fact that another court might have imposed a different sentence was insufficient to justify appellate intervention.
Khairul Azam was represented by Awang Armadajaya Awang Mahmud and Nur Jehan Abu Bakar, while deputy public prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry appeared for the prosecution.

8d1c4d66f9e1f3b0: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's fiscal deficit is expected to narrow to 3.4 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2027, from a projected 3.5 per cent this year, according to JP Morgan.
The US investment bank said the government was balancing near-term support measures with increasingly binding medium-term fiscal constraints.
These include higher oil prices, rising debt-servicing costs and an elevated starting level of public debt, which could limit fiscal room for further spending.
JP Morgan said the government has progressively reduced the deficit from 6.4 per cent of GDP in 2021 to 3.7 per cent in 2025 via a mix of revenue enhancing and expenditure reducing measures.

"Against the more challenging backdrop, we expect fiscal consolidation to continue, albeit at a slower pace, with 2027 Budget likely to prioritise a reallocation rather than an expansion of overall spending," it said.

The firm expects the budget to reprioritise rather than significantly expand overall spending, with some savings likely to come from a lower projected subsidy bill in 2027 due to lower projected oil prices.
JP Morgan forecasted for the oil prices to hit US$85 per barrel this year and US$63 in 2027.

"In this regard, the government's pre-budget statement indicates that 2027 Budget will focus on alleviating cost-of-living pressures, including through the existing cash transfer and subsidy frameworks, while also maintaining fiscal discipline.

"This could imply a further moderation in development expenditure from the 3.7 per cent of GDP projected for 2026, as revenues are channelled towards household support measures and debt servicing costs," it said.
The firm also said that fiscal pressures have eased since April, but not gone away entirely.

The government had initially budgeted RM15 billion for fuel subsidies in 2026 but now expects total fuel subsidy outlays to reach RM40 billion, implying a RM25 billion increase, down from the RM43 billion increase projected in April.
It said part of this excess subsidy bill should be offset by stronger-than-budgeted revenues, including higher petroleum-related tax receipts and royalties.
"Stronger nominal GDP growth should also help compress the deficit ratio through a larger denominator effect.

"Under our central scenario of eight and nine per cent nominal GDP growth this year, the fiscal deficit could still meet the government's 3.5 per cent of GDP target even with a modest RM2 billion-3 billion overshoot in the nominal deficit.

"Even so, we expect some residual shortfall to remain, necessitating additional revenue-mobilising measures, such as a special dividend from Petroliam Nasional Bhd, to achieve the fiscal target," it said.
0679f1e13f90ee18: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The High Court today dismissed an application by Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, to stay the execution of a judgment ordering him to pay RM280,000 in damages to former Penang Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng and his son.

Judge Roslan Mat Nor, in dismissing the application, ruled that the defendant had failed to establish any special circumstances warranting a stay of execution pending the disposal of his appeal, which was filed on June 2.

“The defendant claimed that he would succeed in his appeal and that the appeal would be rendered academic if the judgment sum was paid now. The defendant also contended that he would face bankruptcy proceedings if the plaintiffs executed the judgment.
“These reasons do not assist the court in exercising its discretion to grant a stay,” he said, and ordered Wan Muhammad Azri to pay RM5,000 in costs.

On May 19 this year, the court ruled that Wan Muhammad Azri was liable for defamation and ordered him to pay RM280,000 in damages to Guan Eng and Clint Lim Way Chau over the latter's posts alleging that Way Chau was detained in Singapore for purportedly bringing in RM2 million in undeclared cash in 2020.
The court ordered the defendant to pay global damages of RM200,000 and costs of RM30,000 to Guan Eng as well as damages of RM80,000 and costs of RM10,000 to the second plaintiff (Way Chau).

The duo filed the suit on April 19, 2020, alleging that the defendant had posted defamatory statements on his Facebook page claiming that Way Chau was detained at Changi Airport on February 29, 2020, for bringing in RM2 million in undeclared cash.

Guan Eng said the defendant, who uploaded the post under the name ‘Papa Azri’ on March 14, 2020, also claimed that Guan Eng had travelled to Singapore on February 29, 2020, after the alleged detention.
Lawyer Simon Murali attended today's proceedings, representing both plaintiffs, while lawyer Fazilah Jaafar represented Wan Muhammad Azri. — Bernama
4b463db6bfe0caac: BERLIN, Sept 17 — Two German state elections Sunday could deal a double blow to embattled Chancellor Friedrich Merz, two weeks after his party suffered a stunning defeat at the hands of the far-right AfD.
Tight races for power – each with their own unique electoral dynamics – are expected in the city-state of Berlin and the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

The Alternative for Germany is expected to make strong gains in both, a fortnight after it trounced Merz’s centre-right CDU by a margin of almost 44 to 17 per cent in the ex-communist eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.

The AfD triumph badly rattled Merz and fuelled speculation that the 70-year-old leader, who took power in May last year, may not sit out the end of his four-year term as leader of Europe’s top economy.

Amid speculation about a potential change at the top, eight CDU state premiers closed ranks Wednesday and declared jointly that Germany needs “stability now more than ever” rather than “discussions about personnel”.
Merz has vowed to reboot Germany’s flagging economy, rearm the country to deter a hostile Russia and contain irregular immigration to soothe voters’ fears and lure them away from the AfD.
Instead, the AfD now leads nationwide polls, Merz’s personal approval ratings hover around 10 per cent, and his coalition with the centre-left SPD is increasingly torn by infighting.
“In Merz’s case, we are now observing the possibility of a tipping point – an implosion rather than a slow erosion of authority,” said Oliver Lembcke, a political scientist at Ruhr University Bochum.
“When election defeats, poor personal ratings and internal party doubts reinforce one another, political authority can collapse very quickly.”
Two close election battles
In one election Sunday, in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Merz’s party is an onlooker to the main battle between the SPD of popular state premier Manuela Schwesig and the AfD.

While the AfD was polling at 37 per cent against the SPD’s 35 in the latest INSA survey, Merz’s CDU, at just seven per cent, may drop dangerously close to the five-per cent hurdle needed to stay in the state parliament.
A CDU crash below that line would be a historic first and heap enormous pressure on Merz.

If the CDU “were indeed to fail to clear the five-percent threshold, I consider it quite likely that Mr Merz would be pressured by his party to step down,” said Ursula Muench of the Academy for Political Education in Tutzing.
“Barring such a drastic turning point, I do not foresee this happening for the time being.”
In Berlin, the ruling CDU is running a neck-and-neck race against the far-left Die Linke, which is popular with many young people and promises drastic steps to solve a dire housing crisis.
A CDU defeat in the capital would be another black eye for Merz.

The AfD is meanwhile expected also to do well in Berlin, although it is set to remain shut out of power in both states because all other main parties have agreed on a “firewall” of non-cooperation with it.
‘Dissatisfaction running high’
Whoever wins either poll, the AfD is sure to again channel voter discontent with the mainstream parties.
“I do hope they vote for the AfD here, I can tell you, because the CDU have been in power for years and they haven’t got their act together,” said Berlin retiree Manuela Schmidt, 63.
She pointed to poverty-stricken pensioners collecting bottles off the streets to collect the deposits.

“They’ve worked for 45 years, get a pension of 500-something (euros per month), and go out at night to collect bottles, only to be driven away by foreigners in the end... and that simply can’t go on,” Schmidt told AFP.
Merz – bracing for a tough Sunday evening – has scheduled a CDU executive committee meeting then to quickly discuss the election results and the way forward.
He also cleared his calendar for the coming week by scrapping plans to travel to the UN General Assembly, sending his foreign minister to New York instead.
“Dissatisfaction is evidently running high” in the CDU camp, said Muench, adding, however, that cooler heads might eventually prevail to avoid boosting the AfD under co-leader Alice Weidel.

“It must surely be clear to level-headed CDU politicians that replacing the CDU chairman and chancellor would not serve their own interests,” she said. “It would just fuel the AfD’s pipe dreams of a ‘Chancellor Alice Weidel’.” — AFP

24807d9c5f36a9bd: KLUANG, Sept 17 — A palm oil mill in Kluang has been identified as the source of pollution in Sungai Sembrong and ordered to halt operations immediately.

The directive was issued by the Kluang branch of the Department of Environment (DoE) following an investigation and inspection of the facility after pollution in the river was first detected on Monday.
“Further investigation revealed a pump malfunction at the mill’s effluent treatment pond, causing an overflow of oil-contaminated effluent into Sungai Sembrong.

“The mill has been ordered to halt operations immediately and is required to carry out cleanup and repair works. Follow-up action on the suspension of its licence is also underway,” the DoE said in a statement today.
Dead fish and prawns had previously been found along stretches of Sungai Sembrong, with the pollution reportedly affecting the livelihoods of nearby Orang Asli villagers.
The DoE reminded industries, particularly palm oil mill operators, to strictly comply with requirements under the Environmental Quality Act 1974 and the department’s licensing conditions.

It warned that stern action, including the suspension or revocation of licences, would be taken against any breach of the Act that causes environmental pollution or threatens drinking water supplies or public health.
74b951bfa2ee851b: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) has appointed Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd's (BPHB) wholly-owned subsidiary Bintulu Port Sdn Bhd (BPSB) as an approved port operator for Bintulu Port for 30 years, from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2056.
BPHB said the appointment was approved by the Sarawak legislative assembly.

“The appointment is set out in the Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) (Appointment of Approved Port Operator) Notification, 2026, published in the Sarawak Government Gazette, Part II, dated September 10, 2026. The notification was made under section 12(2)(a) of the Port Authorities Ordinance, 1961,” it said in a stock exchange filing.

On June 23, 2026, the Sarawak Ministry of Infrastructure and Port Development notified BPSB that the government had approved in principle the appointment of BPSB as the approved port operator for Bintulu Port under Section 12(2)(a) of the Port Authorities Ordinance, 1961.

BPHB said BPSB “shall perform, carry out or provide the port undertakings at Bintulu Port subject to full compliance with the ordinance and any by-laws, regulations or subsidiary legislation made under it.”
BPSB will also carry out the terms and conditions of the Heads of Agreement (HOA) dated July 27, 2026, entered into between the Sarawak state government, Bintulu Port Authority and BPSB, it added.

“The HOA terms and conditions shall continue to apply until the Port Operation Concession Agreement (POCA) is duly executed by those parties. Upon execution, the POCA shall be binding on BPSB and govern its operation of Bintulu Port,” said BPHB. — Bernama
20f289b90d94fda7: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will continue to have a presence on the LPGA Tour next season after Mirabel Ting secured her card for 2027 in her first full year as a professional.
The 20-year-old Sarawakian has enjoyed a superb rookie campaign on the Epson Tour, winning twice and currently leading the Race for the Card standings.
Her promotion means Malaysia are already assured of representation next year at the pinnacle of women's professional golf, with the possibility of having two players competing on the LPGA Tour.
Natasha Andrea Oon, Malaysia's sole representative this season, is battling to retain her playing status after spending much of the previous two years sidelined by injury.
Competing under a medical exemption this season, Natasha is currently 127th in the Race to CME Globe.
Mirabel, meanwhile, has been in red-hot form on the LPGA's developmental circuit, recording five consecutive top-10 finishes in her most recent starts.
She finished runner-up at the Hartford HealthCare Women's Championship before claiming her maiden title at the Smoky Mountain Championship in August.

A tied-10th finish at the Wildhorse Ladies Golf Classic followed before Mirabel captured her second title at the Dream First Bank Charity Classic and then finished tied fourth at last week's Guardian Championship.
Her performances have made an LPGA Tour dream shared by her family a reality.
"It's kind of my dream since I was a little kid," Mirabel told the Epson Tour.

"And obviously my grandfather's dream, my dad's dream, my grandmother's dream, and my sister's dream too. So, part of wanting to be on the LPGA is also because of her. I want to be there and do my best."
Mirabel lost her father Thomas to a heart attack during her freshman year at Augusta University in 2022, while her grandfather died shortly before she made her professional debut last year.
"This has been their longest dream," she said of her father and grandfather.
"So, to the two of them, I'd say: I've done it, and I'll continue working hard."

With her LPGA card secured, Mirabel still has two Epson Tour events remaining, beginning with the Murphy USA El Dorado Shootout in Arkansas tomorrow before the season-ending Epson Tour Championship at Indian Wells on Oct 1-4.
She will then return home to lead the five-strong Malaysian challenge at the US$3 million Maybank Championship at Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club from Oct 29-Nov 1.
Mirabel, who finished tied 12th as an amateur in 2024 — the best result by a Malaysian in the tournament's history — will be joined by Natasha, Kelly Tan, Jeneath Wong and Liyana Durisic.
The field will include defending champion Miyu Yamashita, world No. 2 Jeeno Thitikul, Lydia Ko, Ruoning Yin, Haeran Ryu, Charley Hull and former champion Celine Boutier.
e54112b0eb421205: KUALA LUMPUR: A technician charged with causing grievous hurt to a businessman during a restaurant attack has submitted a representation to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC), seeking a reduction of the charge against him.
Lawyer Muhamad Firdaus Jumaludin, who represents Lai Kae Bin, 33, said the representation was submitted on Sept 2 for a review of the charge under Section 326 of the Penal Code.
Firdaus said Lai had instructed him to seek a lesser charge, as he felt the existing charge was too serious.

"We went through the evidence and did not see any intention on his part to commit the act. It happened in the spur of the moment," he said after proceedings before Sessions Court judge Noor Aini Yusof today.
Lai is one of three men charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt to businessman Andrew Teh, 47, using dangerous weapons at Restoran Hing Kee Bakuteh in Jalan Kepong at 2am on May 7.
The other two accused are carpenter Wong Weng Luen, 49, and memorial centre worker Wan Ken Fei, 30.
All three have pleaded not guilty to the charge.
Only Lai and Wan were present in the dock during today's proceedings, while several of their family members sat in the public gallery.
Wong was not brought to court as he is currently undergoing psychiatric assessment at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak, following a court order last month.
Deputy public prosecutor Adiba Iman Hassan said the prosecution had yet to receive Wong's psychiatric report as the hospital required another month to complete the assessment.
She also confirmed that the A-GC had received Lai's representation, which was still under review.
"Besides the psychiatric report, we have yet to receive the closed-circuit television (CCTV) forensic report and the victim's full medical reports from private and government hospitals.
"I also wish to record that the prosecution has handed over documents to Lai's lawyer," she said.
Noor Aini ordered Wong to remain at the hospital for assessment and fixed Oct 13 for mention of the psychiatric report.
The same date was set for the prosecution to hand over additional documents.
Lawyer Mohammad Arifin Abdul Wahab appeared on behalf of lawyer S. Narasimham, who represents Wan.
Meanwhile, lawyer Keith Moo, who held a watching brief for Teh, said the victim had yet to fully recover and was still receiving hospital treatment.
The attack allegedly stemmed from an incident in which Teh was accused of staring at a man believed to be intoxicated while dining at the restaurant.
Closed-circuit television footage of the several-minute assault later went viral on social media.
The footage showed Teh seated at a table before one of the men approached and began attacking him.
Two others then joined in, initially appearing to restrain their friend before taking part in the assault.
Teh was punched, kicked and struck with various objects, including chairs and a kettle, before managing to escape.

fca6a1b3d6fcbcbf: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) today said that a letter dated July 17, 2026, claiming that Cabinet approval had been given for a proposed Private Finance Initiative (PFI) project to widen the North-South Expressway (PLUS) is fake.
In a statement today, PMO stressed that the Prime Minister had never issued or signed the letter and denied any connection with the document or the purported approval.
“PMO has lodged a police report over the forgery of the document and the misuse of the Prime Minister’s name and PMO’s official identity.
“Appropriate legal action will be taken against any party found to be involved,” the statement read.
PMO therefore advised the public not to be deceived by, circulate, or share the fake document. — Bernama
3ec821cccd31d54a: NAGOYA, Sept 17 — Accommodation for Asian Games athletes in Japan is “functional” and efforts are being made to deal with numerous complaints from disgruntled teams, a chief organiser told AFP.
More than 17,000 competitors and officials are expected at the continent’s biggest sporting spectacular, which opens on Saturday in Nagoya.
In a bid to cut costs, organisers are housing athletes and officials in temporary accommodation ranging from a cruise liner and wooden containers to hotel rooms.
The plan has run into immediate problems, with South Korean officials branding the container huts the “worst ever” and saying the beds are too short.
An official from another team told AFP that he entered the facility, took one look at the arrangement and booked a hotel room instead.
Several countries have also complained about a shortage of accommodation.
Speaking ahead of the opening ceremony, organising committee president Hideaki Omura said efforts are being made to ensure athletes are comfortable.
“If there are different opinions then we will respond to them appropriately,” said Omura, who also serves as governor of Aichi prefecture.
“At this point, while we are responding to individual opinions, we have been improving everything as issues arise and we will continue to respond that way.”
Byeon Jun-hyeong, a player with South Korea’s men’s basketball team, posted a video on social media showing a leaking sink and soaked floor in his hut accommodation.
He posted the caption, “Please help us”.
Hundreds of athletes were briefly evacuated from their accommodation last week as record rainfall lashed Nagoya.
About 2,000 people are supposed to stay in the huts.
Cruise control
Omura said plans for the huts, which were built this year, had been given a favourable assessment by a committee of former athletes, including Olympians.
“We explained everything to them and had them take a look around, and they said it looked functional and good,” he said.
About 4,000 athletes and officials will also stay on the Italian cruise ship Costa Serena, which arrived in Nagoya on Tuesday.
Cruise ships have been used previously as accommodation at international sports events but never on this scale.
The Asian Games are taking place at a time when typhoons are common in Japan, and Nagoya has experienced heavy rainfall in recent weeks.
Omura said the priority was to keep athletes and officials on board safe.
“We believe we can provide accommodation that guarantees athletes’ safety and allows them to deliver their best performance,” he said.
Slow sales
Athletes from 45 countries and territories will compete in more than 40 sports across over two weeks.
Omura said ticket sales were going “fairly well”, especially for the marquee events.
But he admitted that lesser-known sports had yet to capture the Japanese public’s imagination.
That includes cricket, which is practically unknown in Japan.
“India have a superstar cricket squad coming and Indian residents in Japan are saying, ‘I can’t believe we get to watch matches like this’, but ticket sales haven’t been very strong,” said Omura.
“A lot of people in Japan have never seen cricket, so I really hope they take this chance and go and watch.”
Events at the Games including basketball and football have been under way since last week.
Omura said he was in attendance as the first action began when Qatar took on Iran in men’s basketball.
After watching a physical contest, Omura said he hoped the Games would help Asia “reaffirm its bonds of friendship through sport”.
“Iran and Qatar are in a situation where missiles are flying back and forth but they can still play basketball together,” he said.
“Without the Asian Games you couldn’t have a game like that.” — AFP
8ced7081da5705c2: KUALA LUMPUR: Jokes that mock, insult, ridicule and demean others are strictly prohibited by and contradicts the teachings of Islam.

Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan said Verse 11 of Surah Al-Hujurat clearly forbids believers from insulting fellow human beings, mocking, calling each other by bad nicknames, and denouncing one another.

"In every speech or address, a leader should elevate mature discourse, focusing on national development and the strengthening of unity, rather than being tainted by sexually suggestive jokes, let alone those that touch upon the sensitivities of other religious institutions.

"The act of turning symbols or figures of any religion into the butt of jokes degrades the values of leadership etiquette and tears apart the inter-religious harmony that has always been upheld in this country," he said in a statement.
Zulkifli said, as leaders who serve as role models for society, particularly those who are Muslims, such lapses in judgment should be realised and addressed properly.
"I urge all parties to refocus on issues concerning the people's interests and cultivate a public discourse based on wisdom, politeness, and high moral values," he said.

He was commenting on the controversy surrounding the speech by Sepang Umno Division chief Datuk Noorazli Said at the party's recent general assembly in which he made a suggestive joke about a priest and a nun.
Noorazli's joke angered many people, with one minister calling for him to be investigated.
Several people also questioned the sincerity of his apology, but Noorazli defended it, saying only God would know what was in a person's heart.
Meanwhile, when met after a function at World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, Zulkifli said anything which went against religious values should be rejected.
He reiterated that no one should joke about anything which touched on religious sensitivities, adding that this was in line with the views of Islamic scholars.

"What we need to do is focus our discourse on matters that strengthen the soul and unity, that bring people together. Malaysians should stay away from anything that goes against these values," he said.
de26eb2c4ed15a5f: SYDNEY, Sept 17 — Australia will reduce migration by curbing “visa hopping”, tightening rules on students and working holiday makers as well as cracking down on overstayers, its interior minister said Thursday, as the far-right surges in the polls.
Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke told the National Press Club in Canberra that immigration was “fundamentally a strength” for Australia, but accepted that housing pressures required changes.

He denied his ruling Labor party was tightening visa rules in response to the rise of One Nation, which has become one of the country’s most popular parties this year with pledges to drastically slash migration. Business groups warned such cuts would cause economic damage.
“We need immigration to soften enough that housing has a chance to catch up,” he said, while stressing the housing shortage was not caused by migrants.

Net overseas migration – the net gain or loss to the population through movement to and from Australia – reached a peak of 538,000 in 2022 after a surge in arrivals when borders re-opened after the Covid-19 pandemic.
Numbers fell to 292,100 in the year to March, data on Thursday showed.
Burke said this was 47 per cent below the post-Covid peak – and that policy changes would help to reach a target of 225,000 for next year.
Australians want to know the government was “taking control” of migration but also “being decent about it”, he said.
Students are the largest group of arrivals, with 753,000 international students in Australia, most from China and India, data shows.
Under the new rules, family members seeking to join students in Australia will face new curbs and it will become harder for students to move between courses to extend their stay, Burke said.

A backlog of applications from the UK for working holiday visas would continue to be processed slowly after a record 80,000 applications – a matter that is under discussion with the UK government, he said.
Working holiday makers in rural areas will enter a ballot to stay for a second or third year, with just 5,000 visas available for the latter.
Family members seeking to visit Australians will have “no further stay” conditions attached to their temporary visas.
Migrants with construction and housing skills will be prioritised for visas, he said.
Australia would return to a policy of a decade earlier in which visa overstayers were given two weeks to leave the country or face detention and deportation, he said.
An additional 100 compliance officers and 250 more beds in immigration detention centres would show there are consequences to overstaying a visa, he said.
But he stressed “this is not the sort of operation that some people have seen on TV happening in other countries” – a nod to hardline immigration policies in the United States.
A third of Australia’s resident population of 27.6 million was born overseas, the latest census data shows. — AFP
e849b3d3bb3b66d1: KUALA LUMPUR: Gas Malaysia Bhd has teamed up with France's Air Liquide Engineering & Construction to explore opportunities in low-carbon hydrogen, carbon dioxide off-take and bio-liquefied natural gas in Malaysia.

797188a408c22086: IPOH, Sept 17 — PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim has hit out at those criticising Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying some were quick to make political statements but lacked the courage to follow through with their actions.

He said while there were political statements suggesting that the country was currently unstable, the government remained committed to ensuring political stability as a foundation for economic stability and, ultimately, the benefit of the people.
“Our priority is to ensure political stability because from there, we can ensure economic stability, which will ultimately benefit the people,” he said.
He spoke to reporters after presenting allocations to non-governmental organisations in the Prime Minister’s Tambun parliamentary constituency at the Penghulu Mukim Hulu Kinta Office here.

Muhammad Kamil, who is also Anwar’s political secretary, said he did not deny that certain groups were deliberately attempting to create political instability to serve the interests and demands of certain leaders within their respective parties.

“Today, what we can assure the people is that the current government, particularly the Prime Minister, is committed to ensuring that all policies and plans can be implemented and that the government works for the good and benefit of the people as a whole,” he said.
He said this remained the case despite some statements appearing to attack Anwar personally.
“Some people are brave enough to talk, but they are not brave enough to act.
“So, we need to assess which leaders are working and which leaders are merely playing politics. I think the people can make a good assessment of that,” he said.

Muhammad Kamil also said there appeared to be confusion among the public when some political figures called for the 16th general election (GE16) to be held soon while at the same time saying they would remain in the government until the end of its term.
“That is something you have to ask that person. In the morning they say one thing, and at night they say another. They are confusing people,” he said.

Muhammad Kamil was responding to recent remarks made during the Umno general assembly, where party president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi challenged Anwar to remove Umno from the unity government and face a confidence vote in Parliament.
Ahmad Zahid was also reported to have reminded coalition partners that Anwar’s administration remained in power with Umno’s support.
“The Prime Minister is the prime minister because of Umno’s support,” Ahmad Zahid was quoted as saying.
Ahmad Zahid was also reported to have backed calls for an earlier general election during the assembly.
a77ccddfba6b76ae: JAKARTA: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi arrived here for a working visit aimed at strengthening Malaysia-Indonesia cooperation in disaster management, including forest and land fires, as well as the halal industry and rural development.

339b0cd15e7989d2: JAKARTA: Indonesia will begin making e-commerce platforms collect income taxes from sellers starting Oct 1, a month earlier than previously announced, local media reported on Thursday, citing the tax chief.
The move reverses a delay ordered by the previous finance minister and follows a shake-up at the top of the finance ministry this week.
The finance ministry and the tax office did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Some of the biggest platforms operating in Southeast Asia's largest economy were originally tasked by the tax office to start collecting taxes from sellers beginning in August, but then-finance minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa ordered a delay on Aug 5 because of concern it might hurt purchasing power.
The next day, the tax office said the policy would be delayed to Nov 1 and promised taxes that were already paid would be refunded.
Purbaya was sacked this week and his deputy, veteran technocrat Suahasil Nazara, was named as President Prabowo Subianto's third finance minister in less than two years.

"God willing, we will immediately activate the regulation and implementation. They are ready, we are ready," the head of the finance ministry's tax department, Bimo Wijayanto, said, according to CNBC Indonesia, adding the collection will begin Oct 1. "There's no drama."
Sources told Reuters Purbaya had clashed with top officials in his ministry prior to his removal, including with Bimo, over the reshuffling of hundreds of officials at the ministry.

​Tokopedia, controlled by ByteDance's TikTok and ​partly owned by Indonesia's biggest tech company GoTo, together with Sea Limited's Shopee, the Alibaba-backed Lazada, and Blibli, had previously been appointed as tax collectors.

Indonesia has a booming e-commerce industry, with an estimated gross merchandise value of US$71 billion in 2025 that is expected to grow to US$140 billion by 2030, according to a report by Google, Singapore state investor Temasek and consultancy Bain & Co.
ba233a1ccef22164: GENEVA: The planet's water cycle is becoming increasingly erratic, swinging between too little and too much, the UN warned Thursday, with an unprecedented El Nino expected to exacerbate the long-term trend.
Last year was among the driest for the world's rivers in over three decades, the UN's World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said in a report.
In 2025 - one of the warmest years on record - glaciers also shrank across all regions, even as groundwater levels in many parts of the world are in multi-year decline, it found.

Overall, the WMO's annual State of Global Water Resources report showed that the Earth's freshwater storage - the total amount of water stored in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, vegetation and ice and snow - continued a decade-long decline.
Some elements of the water cycle change rapidly - like precipitation, river flow and soil moisture, responding to weather within days or weeks.

WMO secretary-general Celeste Saulo voiced particular concern about the decline in "slow reserves", like groundwater and glaciers, which she said had traditionally served as the planet's "savings account".
They have served as "a buffer that absorbs bad years so that a single drought or a single dry season does not translate directly into a water crisis", she told reporters.
'Spending our reserves'
Now, "we are depleting that savings account", she warned. "We are spending our reserves," she said.
Glaciers have also been shrinking at a precipitous rate, with 2025 marking the fourth consecutive year where they shed significant ice mass across all regions.

Between 2023 and 2025, the report estimated that glaciers lost a cumulative global glacier mass of 1,400 gigatonnes of water - roughly equal to the water required to fill 560 million Olympic-sized swimming pools, or about a third of the world's annual freshwater withdrawals.
"Groundwater tells a similar story: nearly two-thirds of monitored wells worldwide showed conditions outside the historical norm in 2025," Saulo said.
She highlighted that this was happening in parallel with "more water-related disasters".
In particular, she pointed to the current El Nino pattern, which is expected to be the strongest since comparable records began four decades ago.

El Nino is the warm phase of a natural climate cycle that occurs every two to seven years and is characterised by above average ocean temperatures across the Pacific, and brings worldwide changes in winds and rainfall patterns and erratic weather.
"The strengthening El Nino will increase the risk of drought in some areas, and flooding in others," Saulo cautioned.
'Abnormal'
Already before El Nino hit, rivers worldwide were showing "abnormal" flows, WMO said, with 2025 among the three driest years for rivers in 35 years.
For a seventh year in a row, river basins experiencing "normal" conditions were in a clear minority globally in 2025.
Only around 36% saw normal flows, while an equal percentage saw below-normal discharge conditions and 21% were above normal, the report found.
The WMO stressed the importance of good data to map the developments in the water cycle, warning that significant gaps remained in hard-hit areas.
"Weather respects no borders, and this is especially true for water," Saulo said, arguing for the importance of "shared data, shared standards and shared early warnings".
"A river basin is fed by water upstream, often in another country," she pointed out.
And "a glacier disaster in one country can lead to devastation in another, as we saw with the recent tragedy of China and Nepal," she added.
03bdd66ec09960ce: KUALA LUMPUR: Artiste Elizabeth Tan is continuing her journey to have children with her husband, Dr Siew Jim Ding, through in vitro fertilisation, following several unsuccessful attempts to conceive.
The 32-year-old hopes to have at least two children before she turns 35, largely because she wants her ageing parents to spend quality time with their future grandchildren.

"My husband and I started trying when I was 30. If possible, I'd love to have two children before I turn 35, but right now, I don't even have one," Tan said during a recent press conference for her upcoming horror film, Pemuja Syaitan.
"My parents are getting older, and I really want them to see my children grow up. I'm doing this for them as much as for myself," she added.
However, Tan is keeping a grounded mindset and leaving the outcome in God's hands.
She revealed that the initial stage of treatment—egg retrieval—will begin this year, while the embryo transfer is planned for next year.
Her professional commitments are also playing a role in her timeline, as she plans to wrap up a major film project before moving forward with the transfer.
"I'm weighing up whether to proceed with the embryo transfer now or finish the film first, but I think the film needs to come first. Once filming wraps up, I'll do the transfer," she explained.

Tan admitted that IVF was far from her first choice, noting that most couples would prefer to conceive naturally. Before deciding on IVF, she underwent intrauterine insemination (IUI) twice, though neither attempt succeeded.
"Nobody chooses IVF as their first option. If possible, everyone wants to conceive naturally," she shared.
"I'm trying not to get my hopes up too much. We've tried every single month without success, and doing IVF doesn't automatically guarantee a result."
Tan previously shared that she had suffered two miscarriages, both occurring at around seven weeks.
She and Dr Siew tied the knot on March 21, 2021.
On the work front, Tan is set to star in Pemuja Syaitan, which marks the directorial debut of actress Liyana Jasmay.
Also starring Zul Ariffin, Nadhir Nasar, and Aila Azizul, the film is produced by Mermaid Studios in collaboration with Suraya Filem Production & Distribution.
Pemuja Syaitan is scheduled to hit cinemas nationwide on Oct 15.
3690945e3f9c72e2: PETALING JAYA: The Muar High Court has set aside a man’s conviction and 20‑year jail sentence for raping his stepchild after the sessions court failed to provide written grounds for its decision.

Judicial commissioner S Kalyana Kumar ordered a retrial of the case before another sessions court judge, saying the High Court could not determine if the conviction was safe without the trial judge's grounds of judgment.
The 42-year-old accused was previously convicted of raping his stepchild at a house in Simpang Renggam on Aug 8, 2022. He was sentenced to 20 years in prison and 10 strokes of the cane.
He appealed to the High Court to set aside the conviction and sentence.
In allowing the appeal, Kalyana noted that the trial judge who convicted the accused had already retired.
He added that the judge did not provide any "meaningful oral reasoning" at the end of the case for either the prosecution or defence.
"The records only show a brief decision, that a prima facie case had been proven, and that the prosecution had proven its case beyond reasonable doubt.
"In this appeal, absolutely no written grounds of judgment has been provided," said the judge, adding that the written grounds are mandatory for appeals under the Criminal Procedure Code.
He said another issue with this case was that the trial was heard before two different judges.
The first judge had heard from key prosecution witnesses, including the complainant, while the second judge heard from the investigating officer and defence.
"The problem here is that the second sessions court judge did not see or hear the testimony of the complainant, who was the main prosecution witness," he added.
The accused was represented by Mandave Singh Gill while deputy public prosecutor Siti Asmah Zainal Ariffin prosecuted.
446d1ebf6596f478: ALOR STAR: Water supply for padi cultivation in the Muda area is facing a major challenge in Season 2/2026, with water levels at the three dams under the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) averaging just 35.76 per cent.
MADA said the water storage level at Pedu Dam was at 36.99 per cent, followed by Ahning Dam at 44.33 per cent and Muda Dam at 11.88 per cent.
It said limited reserves meant irrigation for the coming planting season would depend heavily on rainfall.

"This situation is expected to become more challenging following projections by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), which show the probability of the El Nino phenomenon rising to 96 per cent towards the end of the year.
"The phenomenon has the potential to develop into a stronger phase, bringing hot, dry weather and increasing the risk of rainfall deficits.
"These conditions are expected to pose a major challenge to water availability and padi cultivation activities in the Muda area," Mada said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, the Mada Water Supply and Padi Cultivation Committee meeting yesterday set the Season 2/2026 planting schedule for the entire 99,489-ha area to begin on Sept 23.
The sowing date for phase one is set from Sept 23 to Nov 4, followed by phase two from Oct 3 to Nov 14, while phase three will run from Oct 13 to Nov 24.
"For Season 1/2026, planting activities involving a total area of 100,641 ha are currently in the final flowering and harvesting stages.
"As of Sept 16, pre-saturation progress reached 100 per cent, land preparation hit 99 per cent, and planting reached 98.4 per cent, while the harvest rate reached 9.3 per cent," it said.
Mada urged farmers to use existing water resources prudently to mitigate the risks.
At the same time, Mada will support irrigation needs in affected areas by maximising the operation of drainage water recycling pumps and mobile pumps on site.
"Mada also requests farmers to adhere to the designated planting schedule and avoid water waste to ensure the continuity of padi production in the Muda area," it said.

ab4397393a22d7ef: PETALING JAYA, Sept 17 — Datuk Ab Ghani Hassan was elected as the Football Association of Malaysia (FAM) president for the remainder of the 2025-2029 term after securing a majority of the votes at the FAM Executive Committee Election today.

afac531fe953e832: WASHINGTON: US lawmakers approved broad new sanctions on Wednesday designed to squeeze Russia over its war in Ukraine, sending the legislation to President Donald Trump after months of delay.

The Republican-led House of Representatives passed the package by 262-159, giving a final congressional green light to the most substantial US legislative effort against Moscow since Trump returned to office.
Trump has said he will sign the measure, which sailed through the Senate in an 86-11 vote last month.

The legislation targets Russia's energy and defense sectors, President Vladimir Putin and other senior officials, as well as Moscow's so-called shadow fleet of tankers used to circumvent Western sanctions.

It also gives Trump authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian oil and gas -- including potentially China and India -- in an effort to choke off revenue financing Moscow's war.
But its sweeping tariff powers produced an unusual split among Democrats, who overwhelmingly support Ukraine but have resisted handing Trump greater authority over trade.
Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, called the bill "deeply flawed."

"White House lawyers drafted the current text to maximize President Trump's authority to impose new import taxes on the American people, and to minimize any obligation to actually impose new sanctions on Russia or its enablers," he said.
Meeks said he would support the legislation if the secondary tariff provisions were removed, but Republicans rejected amendments aimed at narrowing them.
Pressure on Putin
Dozens of Democrats nevertheless backed the measure, offsetting opposition from a handful of Republicans who objected to sanctions on free-market or non-interventionist grounds.
Supporters argue that tougher economic pressure is needed, with Russia's full-scale invasion grinding through its fifth year and no peace settlement in sight.

The House vote was celebrated by pro-Ukraine activists, who pointed to Russian attacks continuing, including drone strikes on Wednesday on civilian transport in the south that officials in Kyiv said killed five people.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had urged Congress to pass the sanctions package, saying greater pressure was needed to force Moscow toward negotiations.
"So now Putin is losing 30,000 his soldiers per month... it's many losses, but he doesn't want to stop this war," Zelensky said during a July trip to Washington that included a meeting with Trump.
"So now initiative (is) not in the hands of Putin."
India said on Thursday it would continue buying oil "through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics."
Moscow is one of New Delhi's most important strategic partners and military suppliers.
The bill would also target companies and foreign actors supporting Russia's military and extend sanctions involving Iran.
Trump has generally preferred to retain control over sanctions and tariffs rather than have Congress dictate policy, helping delay the measure for more than a year.
Its sponsor, Republican senator Lindsey Graham -- who died suddenly in July -- had pushed the legislation since April 2025.
Wednesday's vote came just before House lawmakers were due to leave Washington to campaign ahead of November's midterm elections.

"Once the bill is quickly signed and becomes law, we hope for strong US enforcement to finally end the cash flows to the Kremlin's war chest," said Svitlana Romanko, executive director of Ukrainian energy lobby group Razom We Stand.
"Every day of delay is a day we in Ukraine must bury more people."
241b7421e0c840fa: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 17 — The date for the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly to pave the way for the state election has yet to be set, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.

Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said several state administrative matters needed to be resolved first to ensure all plans proceeded smoothly before the assembly was dissolved.

He was speaking after officiating the 2026 Melaka State-level Senior Citizens Day, Persons with Disabilities (PwD) Day and Children's Day celebration in conjunction with the Tanjung Bidara constituency's Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat (WRUR) programme here.
Ab Rauf said the date would be announced to the media and the public once it had been finalised.

On Tuesday, allegations went viral on WhatsApp claiming that Melaka Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam had signed the Melaka State Assembly dissolution document together with Ab Rauf during a meeting at the Guest Room of the Chief Executive Officer's Office at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh.
The Melaka State Assembly has 28 seats, while the current state government's mandate expires on December 31. — Bernama
50b4724688ff24d9: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Court of Appeal today allowed the prosecution’s application to stay the hearing of additional evidence from a key prosecution witness in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s corruption case involving the RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid project.

A three-member panel led by Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli granted the application after Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Asnawi Abu Hanipah informed the court that Rosmah did not object to the request.
“With the consent of both parties, we allow the application to stay the Court of Appeal’s order dated September 1 until the prosecution’s appeal is disposed of by the Federal Court.
“We hope the parties will inform the High Court of the Federal Court’s decision as soon as it is delivered to facilitate case management at the High Court.

“The court has fixed October 7 for case management via e-Review and vacated the hearing for the main appeal originally scheduled for this October,” said Azhahari, who sat with Judges Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and K. Muniandy.
On September 1, the Court of Appeal allowed Rosmah’s application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence.
The panel subsequently ordered that the additional evidence involving the 16th prosecution witness, businessman Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, be heard before a High Court judge.
Earlier, Mohd Asnawi said today’s proceedings had initially been fixed for the hearing of the application to stay the execution of the High Court order.

“However, this morning, the parties held discussions, and we were informed that the respondent does not object to the application to stay the execution of the previous court order until the prosecution’s appeal at the Federal Court is heard and decided.

“For the court’s information, we filed a notice of appeal on September 4,” said Mohd Asnawi, who is handling the case with Deputy Public Prosecutors Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib and Mohamad Mustaffa P Kunyalam.
Lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, representing Rosmah, confirmed that the defence did not object to the application.

“I confirm that there have been serious discussions regarding this application. Given that the new evidence involves a key witness in the case and the prosecution itself has given an assurance that it will expedite the appeal proceedings at the Federal Court, we have no objection.

“In the interest of both parties, it is appropriate for the appeal at the Federal Court to be heard and decided first,” he said, adding that the parties would attend the High Court proceedings this afternoon to update the court on the status of the appeal at the Court of Appeal.
Rosmah, 74, had applied to adduce additional evidence comprising a police report and a statutory declaration affirmed by businessman Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah.

In the statutory declaration, Rayyan Radzwill alleged, among other things, that he was pressured by the prosecution during the trial, and presented documentary material challenging the credibility of his testimony.
On September 1, 2022, the High Court convicted Rosmah of three corruption charges under Section 16(a)(A) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
She was found guilty of soliciting RM187.5 million and receiving RM6.5 million from former Jepak Holdings managing director Saidi Abang Samsudin through her former aide, Datuk Rizal Mansor.

The gratification was an inducement for Rosmah to assist Jepak Holdings in securing a RM1.25 billion hybrid solar project from the Ministry of Education to supply electricity to 369 rural schools in Sarawak.
Rosmah was sentenced to 10 years in prison for each charge, to run concurrently, and fined RM970 million. She was granted a stay of execution pending her appeal. — Bernama
5b3a57b4fb903db6: PUTRAJAYA: The process of issuing the new-generation MyKad went smoothly today, with an encouraging response from the public, National Registration Department (NRD) Identity Card Division director Muhammad Asraf Sukadi said.
He said the number of applicants for MyKad replacement at NRD Putrajaya had increased to more than 300 this morning, compared with about 100 on a normal day.
"The response has been quite encouraging. There are more people than usual. This morning alone, the registration numbers were already above 300 and many are waiting for the new MyKad.

"Alhamdulillah, there have been no problems so far and everything is going smoothly. At NRD Putrajaya, it takes about 30 minutes to get a new MyKad if there are no problems, while for 12-year-old children, it takes an average of one hour," he told reporters after inspecting the implementation of the new-generation MyKad issuance process today.
Asraf said the public had also given positive feedback on the new MyKad.
On the QR code on the MyKad, he said it could only be accessed by enforcement agencies, demonstrating that its security was at the highest level.
"The QR code can only be used by enforcement agencies, currently NRD. So, the QR code cannot be read by an ordinary phone camera.
"This is to obtain information and also for enforcement purposes, to verify whether the person is the MyKad holder or not," he said.
He advised the public not to rush to replace their MyKad with the new-generation card as the existing MyKad can still be used for various transactions.
"Many may experience FOMO (Fear of Missing Out) and want to replace theirs. As the Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail announced, people should not rush to the NRD," he said.
Starting today, applications for the new-generation MyKad can be made at 40 NRD branches equipped with printing facilities, with the cards ready on the same day.
At NRD branches without printing facilities, applications for the new-generation MyKad can still be made, with the cards ready within five working days.

The new-generation MyKad is equipped with security features including a Dynamic Security Hologram and Transparent Window on the front, as well as an Enforcement QR Code and Dual Interface Chip on the back.
696008d088dd5bb8: SHAH ALAM: The High Court here has dismissed a couple's bid to have their adopted daughter, whose biological parents are unknown, declared a Malaysian citizen by operation of law.
Judicial commissioner Asmah Musa ruled that the couple had failed to establish the constitutional requirements necessary for the girl to acquire citizenship.
The girl, who was born in Selangor on Nov 23, 2011, has been raised by the couple since infancy and was formally adopted by them in June last year.
However, her post-adoption birth certificate continued to record her citizenship status as "non-citizen".
In her grounds of judgment, Asmah said the couple relied on three constitutional routes to establish the girl's citizenship.
Their principal argument was that she was an abandoned newborn and should benefit from the presumption under Section 19B, Part III of the Second Schedule to the Federal Constitution.
The provision states that a newborn child "found exposed" in any place is presumed, until the contrary is shown, to have been born there to a mother permanently resident there.
The couple also argued that the girl qualified as a citizen as she was born in Malaysia and had not acquired the citizenship of any other country within one year of her birth.
Alternatively, they contended that the word "parents" under the Constitution should encompass them as her lawful adoptive parents, both of whom are Malaysian citizens.
However, Asmah said Section 19B could not be applied merely because the girl's biological parents were unknown.
"Section 19B is not a universal presumption applicable whenever biological parents are unknown.
"Its language begins with a factual condition: there must be a 'newborn child found exposed in any place'.
"Before the consequences of the presumption arise, the evidential foundation for engaging the provision must exist," she said in her grounds of judgment dated Sept 10.
The court heard that the couple had been informed that a baby girl was available for adoption and later went to Klang following an arrangement.
While waiting in their vehicle, an elderly woman approached them carrying the baby and directly handed her to them.
Asmah said this was materially different from a situation where a newborn was found abandoned.
"What occurred before that direct handover remains unknown."
She said there was a distinction between proving that biological parents were unknown and proving that a newborn had been "found exposed" within the meaning of the Constitution.
"Unknown parentage may be a consequence of abandonment.
"It is not, without more, conclusive proof of the particular foundational fact required by section 19B," she said.
The court also rejected the couple's argument that the girl qualified for citizenship under Section 1(e), Part II of the Second Schedule as she was born in this country.
Asmah said existing Court of Appeal authority required an applicant to positively establish that he or she had not acquired citizenship of another country through biological lineage.
"Her biological parents remain unidentified.

"That fact is not proof that they were foreigners; equally, under the existing appellate approach, it is not positive proof that she was incapable of acquiring another citizenship through them," she said.
The couple had also argued that the National Registration Department (NRD) unlawfully deprived the girl of citizenship when her registration was changed to "non-citizen."
The judge said the claim could not succeed as the couple had first failed to establish that she possessed Malaysian citizenship by operation of law.
Asmah also acknowledged the serious practical consequences faced by the girl, who has been raised in Malaysia, has no presently identified foreign citizenship and remains registered as a non-citizen.
However, she said sympathy or hardship could not replace the constitutional requirements.
